note: Existing-source, strict-license-screened public gallery. Additional historical photos remain held from this site. Anatomy overlays are teaching annotations, not a separate verified voucher determination.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — SLIM, CONTRACTED HEAD
tiles.details: Source-identified wild plants (gallery 1 and 4) now actually show ground-level tufted grassy growth and flowering culms, followed by three original photographed narrow flowering heads (5–7). A narrow panicle favors slim tridens, but plant-base photos do not expose knotty roots or rhizomes; purple hue and silhouette alone do not determine the species.
tiles.short: Narrow upright panicle 7–20(25) cm long but only 0.3–0.8 cm wide.
tiles.status: TRUE LIVING BUNCH AND ATTACHED FLOWERING HEAD SOURCE PHOTOS; ACTUAL EXPOSED ROOT CROWN MISSING

tiles.heading: 02 · PERENNIAL BASE, COLLAR AND TRUE LIGULE
tiles.details: Photos 1–4 show actual ground-level clusters of blades and lower sheathing parts beside fingers. These let the crew locate the true collar on a field plant but DO NOT document the opened free ciliate membrane (published 0.5–1 mm), true hair fringe, or connected belowground rhizome. In FNA the bases are knotty/shortly rhizomatous; other resources differ on stolons. Do not assert either from a photograph of in-situ leaf bases.
tiles.short: Knotty, shortly rhizomatous perennial base; 0.5–1 mm membranous, ciliate ligule.
tiles.status: LIVING BASAL SHEATH VIEWS; TRUE LIGULE, CONNECTED ROOTS/RHIZOMES STILL MISSING

tiles.heading: 03 · MEASURE SPIKELETS AND BOTH GLUMES
tiles.details: Count fertile florets in at least three mature spikelets. Flora of North America: lower glume 3–8(10) mm, 1–3-veined; upper glume 4–10 mm, 1–7-veined. Broad glume ranges can reflect infraspecific variation; don't declare variety or species from a single glume measurement. Gallery panels 5 and 7 (1-based; indices 4 and 6) show actual attached flowering units; gallery panel 3 is a lower-leaf/sheath close-up, NOT a spikelet macro. No current panel provides a calibrated glume dissection.
tiles.short: Ripe spikelets 8–13 mm, typically 5–11 florets; glumes persist after florets drop.
tiles.status: REAL ATTACHED SPIKELETS — NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO MEASURED DISSECTION

tiles.heading: 04 · LEMMA HAIRS, PALEA AND AWN
tiles.details: Under 20× examine the dorsal lemma: midvein hairs on basal one-third to one-half, lateral-vein hairs often extending above midlength. Palea about 1–2 mm shorter than lemma. These tiny hair distributions are published diagnostic traits, NOT proven by the existing phone photographs; do not place submillimeter arrows without resolvable pixels.
tiles.short: Fertile lemma 3.5–7 mm; three veins; effectively awnless or minutely pointed.
tiles.status: PUBLISHED MICRO-ANATOMY — NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO DORSAL LEMMA WITH 1-MM BAR

tiles.heading: 05 · BUCKLEY LOOK-ALIKE: COUNT, THEN DISSECT
tiles.details: Slim = slender appressed upright contracted head (actual panels 5–7); Buckley = more open branching head (ACTUAL DIFFERENT-SPECIES panels 8–9). Floret count of five overlaps; only when growth/base/whole panicle fail to separate them, count florets in three mature spikelets and examine dorsal lemma nerve hair placement with 1-mm scale.
tiles.short: Slim: contracted narrow head and usually 5–11 florets; Buckley: open ovate head and usually 3–5.
tiles.status: REAL OTHER-SPECIES COMPARISON — OVERLAPPING COUNTS NEED VERIFIED ANATOMY

tiles.heading: 06 · PUBLIC-READY GATE / TWO HANDOFFS
tiles.details: Four source-checked CC BY living-tuft and basal-sheath photographs (gallery 1–4), three previously archived exact-species flowering-head photographs (gallery 5–7; Rachel CC BY and two Joey Santore CC BY-NC), plus two clearly marked DIFFERENT-SPECIES Buckley comparisons (gallery 8–9). The field photos prove aboveground bunch and narrow attached heads, not an excavated rhizome/root crown, a peeled 0.5–1 mm ciliate true ligule, or measured glumes and dorsal lemma hairs. Keep existing arrows only on resolved gross structures; no microscope claims. The two Joey photographs are conditionally usable only on the noncommercial educational site under their exact NC terms. Publication remains unverified.
tiles.short: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS: seven archived same-species JPEGs and nine gallery panels, not three target JPEGs.

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: SLIM TRIDENTOPSIS (slim tridens): LOOK HERE FIRST for a 7–20(25) cm long, only ~0.3–0.8 cm wide upright panicle with short appressed branches, then trace the flowering culm to its living perennial tuft. Four archived field photographs show aboveground basal blades and sheaths, but NOT exposed roots, rhizomes or a measured inner ligule. Compare Buckley's open, spreading panicle; if ambiguous, count 5–11 florets in mature 8–13 mm spikelets and inspect the three-veined lemma hair pattern. Five florets and 8–10 mm spikelet lengths overlap the two species; color alone is unreliable.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: Gallery photos 1 and 4 are actual source-labeled living narrow grasses IN PLACE at rocky ground level. A tuft is visible; buried knotty rhizome, stolon rooting, and root crown are NOT excavated.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Photos 1–4 show actual ground-level clusters of blades and lower sheathing parts beside fingers. These let the crew locate the true collar on a field plant but DO NOT document the opened free ciliate membrane (published 0.5–1 mm), true hair fringe, or connected belowground rhizome. In FNA the bases are knotty/shortly rhizomatous; other resources differ on stolons. Do not assert either from a photograph of in-situ leaf bases.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Count fertile florets in at least three mature spikelets. Flora of North America: lower glume 3–8(10) mm, 1–3-veined; upper glume 4–10 mm, 1–7-veined. Broad glume ranges can reflect infraspecific variation; don't declare variety or species from a single glume measurement. Gallery panels 5 and 7 (1-based; indices 4 and 6) show actual attached flowering units; gallery panel 3 is a lower-leaf/sheath close-up, NOT a spikelet macro. No current panel provides a calibrated glume dissection.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: Against T. buckleyana, strongly contracted, erect close branches favor mutica over an open ovate head. Counts of 6–11 fertile florets favor mutica, 3–4 favor buckleyana, but five is shared; 8–10 mm spikelet lengths overlap. Avoid treating purple-pink spikelets, a 0.5–1 mm ciliate ligule or short rhizomes as single-character proof.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

panels.label: Slim tridens — narrow, appressed inflorescence

panels.label: COMPARISON — true Buckley tridens OPEN flowering branches (other species)
panels.caption: Eric Knight's verified Texas CC BY image of Buckley tridens, NOT slim tridens. Look at the clearly spread-out lateral flowering branches and separated spikelets. Compare against the attached short upright branches in the preceding narrow mutica panicles, rather than using purple color as an identifier.

memory_rule: BUCKLEYANA = OPEN SPREADING; MUTICA = TIGHT UPRIGHT. Confirm 3–5 versus 5–11 florets and lemma nerve hairs; 5 overlaps.
safety_note: Only basal upper surface and leaf sheaths are newly photographed, no actual exposed rooted knotty crown/rhizome and NO unambiguous true inner 0.5–1 mm ligule. Four new CC BY, three older Rachel/Joey images (Joey CC BY-NC remains restricted), and two Buckley comparisons. Preserve source taxon and county holds.
field_rule: Do not finalize at species if whole-panicle context is absent or floret count sits in overlapping range; dissect true ripe spikelet with scale.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
